transcript.text: Hi, our integrated fridge freezer (behind a kitchen door) - the fridge is around 10 degrees but the freezer seems ok. We had a power cut a week ago, not sure if related. Rented flat, can't really take it out.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is the fan or air channel that moves cold air into the fridge. Is the freezer still cold while the fridge is warm, and is there a thick block of ice on the back wall inside the freezer?
Yes, the freezer's still cold (about -16C) and the fridge is about 10C. There's some frost on the back wall of the freezer but not a thick block, no.

Cold air comes in through vents, often on the back wall inside. Make sure food isn't pressed against them and the shelves aren't packed so tight air can't move. Were the vents blocked or was it over-packed (and have you moved things), or was everything clear?
I can't see any vent in the fridge part, so I'm not sure. It's not overpacked as far as I know. Nothing is pressed against the back wall. Also no burning smell or tripping, if that matters.

Fridge freezers lose their heat through a coil or grille at the back or underneath. Gently dust or vacuum it, and leave a few centimetres of space between it and the wall or cupboards. Was it dusty or pushed against the wall (and have you sorted it), or was it already clean with space round it?
It's integrated behind a cabinet door and screwed into the unit, so I can't pull it out or look at the back. The plinth at the bottom has a vent grille and I can't see anything blocking it.
Keep both doors shut for about 24 hours (only open them briefly) and let it recover. After a day with the doors shut, is it back to cold, or still warm?
Ok, I can try that. It's been about 5 days like this already though, so I'm not sure a day with the doors shut will change much. What should I do if it's still warm after that?

Water inside plus poor cooling usually has one cause: the defrost drain. At the bottom of the back wall inside the fridge there's a small drain hole or channel. If it blocks or ices up, defrost water collects inside and ice can build up behind the back panel and choke the cold air. Clear the hole gently with warm water (a turkey baster or squeezy bottle) or a soft pipe cleaner — nothing sharp. Was the drain hole blocked (and is it clear now), is it blocked or frozen and you couldn't clear it, or was it already clear?
I can't see a drain hole in the fridge, and I haven't noticed any water inside either. Not sure where it would be. Should I just report it to the letting agent instead?

Yes, in a rented flat it's worth reporting it now, because if the fridge came with the property the landlord is usually responsible for repairing it, though that depends on your tenancy agreement. The quick door seal check below is harmless and gives the agent something useful to pass on. Run your fingers round the rubber door seal on each door and look for splits, gaps or a section that has come away, or anything stopping it closing flat. Is the seal torn or come away, was it dirty or folded (and is that sorted), or does it look fine?
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
The fridge door closes ok and the cabinet door moves with it. I can't see any splits in the seal, but I'm not sure what I'd be looking for really. I'll report it to the letting agent anyway.

Check the temperature dial or display: the fridge should be about 3–5°C and the freezer -18°C, and make sure no holiday / eco mode is on. Was a setting wrong or a mode left on (and have you corrected it), or was it all set normally?
The dial inside is on 3 out of 5, and there's no display. I haven't changed it. I don't know if that's the right setting though, should I turn it up?

You can turn it up a notch to 4 without causing harm, but it's unlikely to fix this on its own. It kept the fridge cold at 3 before and the setting hasn't changed, so the dial probably isn't the cause. At the bottom of the back wall inside the fridge there's a small drain hole or channel that carries defrost water away. If it blocks, water collects inside. Clear it gently with warm water (a turkey baster or a squeezy bottle works) or a soft pipe cleaner. Was the drain hole blocked (and is it clear now), is it blocked or frozen and you couldn't clear it, or was it already clear?
